clue.text: Old officer no way better — time in agony

indicators.note: in means the run of short pieces is placed inside the word for agony

parts.note: agony is pain
O looks like a zero, nothing, so it stands for no
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to better something is to cap or top it

explanation.surface: A retired officer finds no way of improving matters and spends his time suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective in the surface but is the verb to top; a post-captain was a Royal Navy rank of Nelson's day.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Royal Navy's title for a full captain of a rated ship in Nelson's era, now a historical rank.

clue.text: Clean up, having dog

parts.note: to mop is to clean a floor

explanation.surface: Someone has to tidy up after their dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal name for a Pomeranian, a small fluffy breed of dog.

clue.text: Little bit of character I found in Russian peasant

indicators.note: offered by means the letters are supplied by the words rich ancestor, running across them

explanation.surface: A wealthy forebear gives the younger generation their openings in life.

clue.text: Ghost, say, appeared quietly to three people

parts.note: piano is the musical direction meaning play quietly

explanation.surface: A ghost silently materialises before a group of three people.

explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ghost is an example of chamber music for keyboard, violin and cello.

clue.text: Concerned with a Tolkien character

clue.text: Poor reception of short novel?

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.walkthrough: A booing audience gives a poor reception; the question mark warns that 'novel' is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeering is a poor reception, and this is the cry an unhappy audience makes.

clue.text: Grow up, governor — manly quality needed for execution

explanation.walkthrough: Execution here is beheading, so COURAGE loses its head C to give OURAGE; 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic command to behave in a more adult way, the same as telling someone to grow up.

clue.text: Said to fight mean? That's without a single benefit

explanation.surface: Fighting is meant to be pointless, and that brings no benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a single benefit' is a cryptic way of saying having two uses, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with two uses does not have just one benefit, hence the playful negative phrasing.

explanation.definitionFit: The volunteer defence force of the Second World War in which Private Pike served in the sitcom.
